notes_list.title: Glucose and Fructose — Important Reactions
notes_list.basic_overview: Glucose and fructose participate in oxidation, reduction, osazone formation and interconversion reactions that reveal structural relationships.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Glucose gives oxidation products depending on reagent strength; reduction gives sorbitol. Fructose can form the same osazone as glucose because the osazone-forming region involves C1/C2.
notes_list.examples: Bromine water selectively oxidizes the aldehyde function of glucose under suitable conditions; HI/red phosphorus historically gives straight-chain hydrocarbon products after extensive reduction.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Reagent identity and pH control selectivity. Strong oxidants can oxidize multiple sites.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Track which carbon atoms are chemically modified. Osazone formation involves reaction of the carbonyl region and two adjacent carbon atoms.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Analytical reaction rates depend on ring-opening equilibrium and reagent concentration.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not infer identical complete structures from identical osazones; stereochemistry outside the osazone-forming region may differ.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
